You're welcome. I deliberately left out some other great stories to keep the list short. The easiest one for new readers to appreciate is probably Cool Air. If I recall correctly Mountains of Madness is the longest, so maybe save it until you've developed some stamina (you'll need it). Shadow Over Innsmouth, and Shadow Out of Time introduce a great deal of lore which relates to other works (and other authors). Other things you might want to know:

  • Lovecraft writes in a verbosely descriptive style which is both light on mundane detail and still very rich with imagery. You'll get used to it, and hopefully come to appreciate it, but some tolerate it better than others.
  • His monsters are the least scary things in his tales. If you're paying attention while reading Rats, Color, and Witch House, you'll understand.
  • He was an unrepentant racist until his death (as far as I know), and it comes out more strongly in some stories than others. Peeps who can't separate the stories from the character of the man may have a bad time. (Specifically, he seems to have held non-whites to be inferior, and that the English were the best white people of all. He also has colorful words for certain "ethnic Europeans", and uneducated people.)
